title: Wipe your own plate with a sponge another robot arm also needs
instruction: Wipe the dirty spots on the plate in front of you with the sponge, leave the other plate alone, and put the sponge back.
context: People who share one sponge or cloth wait for it, use it on their own dishes only and put it back. This checks that a policy can do that beside a second arm that wants the same sponge and cannot be talked to.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A yellow sponge, 4.5 x 7 x 3 cm (60 g), green scouring side down, lies 24 cm forward on the centre line, its length across the table. Two white plates, 16 cm across and 1 cm high, fixed 33 cm forward and 22 cm to either side; each has five brown spots of dirt, 2.4 cm across, drawn on it: one in the middle and four 5 cm out on the diagonals. The other arm waits for the sponge to lie where it started with the controlled arm's hand away from it, takes it, wipes its own plate and puts it back. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: The share of the five spots on the plate in front of the controlled arm that were under the sponge's face while that arm held it pressed on the plate (its underside within 6 mm of the plate), up to 1; halved if the sponge is not back where it started at the end. 0 if the controlled arm wipes the other plate, or if the arms ever touch.
reset_notes: Put the sponge back where it started, green side down, its length across the table. The spots are drawn on; nothing to re-dirty.
fidelity: Approximate. The sponge is a rigid block, so it does not squash; wiping is counted by where it passes, pressed, and the dirt is not removed. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
